body:
Good morning, Bakersfield. The story leading the day is a hard one: a veteran CHP officer was killed Monday evening in a crash on Highway 99 near Tipton, and we have the details below. Closer to home, the night was busy with a structure fire that spread into grass near the Kern-Tulare county line, a grass fire near a church off Auburn Street, and a robbery that ended with one person in custody. Today looks warm and calm — a high near 86, no weather alerts, and air quality sitting at a moderate 72.

## The Kern Overnight

The largest call of the night came at 1:46 a.m., when crews were sent toward County Line Road east of Road 40 after callers reported a large column of smoke and a glow on the horizon. What began as a structure fire had spread into grass and was pushing north at a slow rate of spread, settling at about five acres. Crews anchored off the roadway and worked the heel and flanks while a second unit covered the structures on the south side. Command reported the fire contained and crews in cleanup, and mutual aid requested from Tulare County was canceled.

Earlier, at 10:18 p.m., a patrol, two engines and a battalion were sent to the Morning Drive area, where grass the size of a house was burning near a church off Auburn Street after multiple callers reported it. The full assignment went to the fire. At 1:28 a.m., crews reported light smoke showing from one side of a building in the 900 block of Baker Street and said they were going in to investigate, with incoming units staged and an incident commander assigned. An earlier alarm at the same block was cleared after a crew walked the building and found no audible alarm and no sign of distress or hazard inside.

Deputies had their hands full as well. At 12:47 a.m. a priority one domestic call was broadcast for the 9500 block of Brimhall Road, behind a business; the suspect was described as a man in his 30s in all black who left in a gray pickup, with a second man in dark clothing in an unknown sedan. At 12:52 a.m. deputies were sent to a suspicious person call involving a man with a firearm reported knocking on doors. At 1:14 a.m., a resident reported that a neighbor had come into the home through an unlocked front door, gone as far as a bedroom door and then crossed the street — described as a man 18 to 20 years old in a black shirt and jeans, slim with curly hair. And at 3:01 a.m., several units were called to assist after a robbery was reported; officers put one person in custody, and the victim told officers the robbery happened just east of where the stop was made. The rest of the overnight log was medical aids, alarm calls and traffic stops.

## Today's weather

It's currently 79 degrees at Meadows Field, on the way to a high near 86 this afternoon and a low around 63 tonight. No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County, and air quality is 72 — moderate, which is a reasonable day to be outside if you're not especially sensitive to smoke or dust. No active fires were reported in the county as of this morning beyond the overnight incidents crews handled. Expect a warm, still September day across the valley, with the usual evening cooldown after sundown.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that a Wasco man killed in an early morning shooting has now been identified by the coroner.** The identification closes one small gap in a case that began with gunfire in the early hours, and it gives the man's family and the community a name to hold onto as investigators continue their work. We'll keep following what authorities release about the circumstances.

**According to 23ABC, a veteran CHP officer was killed in the line of duty Monday evening in a crash on State Route 99 near Tipton.** Officer Brian Liles, 44, was riding a department-issued motorcycle northbound just south of Avenue 152 around 5:11 p.m. when it collided with a truck-tractor; the collision ejected him from the motorcycle and he was struck by a passing vehicle. Despite lifesaving efforts, he died at the scene. Liles was a CHP veteran of more than 16 years, serving San Jose, Hayward and Fresno before transferring to Visalia in 2019, and in December 2025 he became one of the first motorcycle officers assigned to the Visalia Area. He is survived by his wife, two children, parents and siblings. The CHP's Central Division Multi-Disciplinary Accident Investigation Team is leading the investigation. This one lands hard across the valley — a motorcycle officer doing routine work on a highway many of us drive every week.

**KGET 17 reports that attorneys clashed as a competency trial was granted for a woman charged in a crash that killed a married couple.** The ruling means the case will pause while the court examines whether the defendant is competent to stand trial — a procedural step, but a significant one for the families of the couple who died. Competency proceedings can shape how, and whether, a case moves forward, and the families involved have already waited a long time for answers.

**Bakersfield Now reports that Congressman Valadao will host Speaker Mike Johnson at a get-out-the-vote rally in Bakersfield on Wednesday.** The visit puts national political attention squarely on the valley in the final stretch before the election, and it's a signal of how much both parties are watching this district. Whatever your politics, it's worth knowing the traffic and attention that will follow a visit of that size midweek.

**23ABC reports that the executive director of the Mission at Kern County will hold a 24-hour addiction awareness conversation for the second year running.** Carlos Baldovinos will sit on a bench for 24 consecutive hours on Oct. 8 and 9 for an event called Conversation on a Bench, and this year he wants to focus on prevention. He told the station that the most powerful moments last year came from family members of people struggling with addiction — parents asking how they can help their son or daughter — and he also saw the other side: people in recovery who reconnected with family, found work and housing, and are thriving. He pushed back on the idea that addiction is a lost cause.

**KGET 17 reports that Jay Thomas Manuel is making a big splash with Jeff Mouse.** We'll be honest with you: that's the headline we have, and we won't pretend to know more than it says. Consider it a curiosity worth a click if you're so inclined.

**Bakersfield Now is asking readers: does hotter weather stop you from attending the Kern County Fair?** It's an informal reader poll, but it touches a real local question — how much September heat shapes whether families spend an evening at the fairgrounds. If you've got an opinion, that's where to register it.

## Something good

For the second year, the director of the Mission at Kern County will hold a 24-hour conversation aimed at raising awareness about addiction, and this year he's adding a focus on prevention. It continues a local effort to keep the community talking about recovery and support — and the stories from last year, from both families in pain and people who came out the other side, are exactly the kind of thing that keeps that conversation honest. If you've been touched by addiction in your own family, you'll recognize the weight of it.

## Coming up this week

The Bakersfield Planning Commission meets Thursday, Oct. 1 at 5:30 p.m. — the main civic meeting on the calendar this week, and the place to be if you want to see what's proposed for your part of town before it's decided.

Looking further out, the Fox Theater has a full slate ahead. The Cults & Classics season pass for 2026-2027 is on sale, and the series brings *Young Frankenstein* to the Fox on Oct. 5. NB RIDAZ takes the stage Oct. 9 for the Ride Till the Wheels Fall Off Tour, FANTASIAS follows Oct. 10, United We Dance brings an all-night festival energy show Oct. 16, and the Boobay & Tekla Comedy Tour lands Oct. 17. If you've been meaning to get downtown for a show, October is the month to do it.

And mark your calendar for Oct. 8 and 9, when the Conversation on a Bench returns to the Mission at Kern County — 24 straight hours of talking about addiction, recovery and prevention, open to anyone who wants to listen or share. Have a good Tuesday, Bakersfield.

top.title: Jay Thomas Manuel makes big splash with Jeff Mouse
